   1| ### 4.2 Card payment with a 3-D Secure challenge
   2| 
   3| This section describes how the Brightwater store takes a card payment when the card issuer asks
   4| for a challenge. Five parties take part. The Checkout page, the Orders API and the Payment service
   5| belong to the Brightwater store. Paylane PSP, the payment provider, and the Issuer ACS, the
   6| challenge page of the card issuer, are external.
   7| 
   8| #### 4.2.1 Steps
   9| 
  10| 1. The Checkout page sends the order to the Orders API.
  11| 2. The Orders API calls the Payment service with `POST /payments`. The request carries the nine
  12|    fields of Table 4.3.
  13| 3. The Payment service asks Paylane PSP to create a payment intent and waits up to 8 s.
  14| 4. Paylane PSP answers `challenge_required` with a `redirect_url`.
  15| 5. The Payment service returns the `redirect_url` to the Orders API.
  16| 6. The Orders API returns the `redirect_url` to the Checkout page.
  17| 7. The Checkout page opens the challenge at the Issuer ACS.
  18| 8. The Issuer ACS sends the browser back to the `return_url` of the Checkout page.
  19| 9. Paylane PSP sends the webhook `payment.succeeded` to the Payment service.
  20| 10. The Payment service answers the webhook with HTTP 200.
  21| 11. The Payment service publishes `payment.confirmed`. The Orders API consumes it and marks the
  22|     order as paid.
  23| 
  24| When step 3 fails with a network error, the Payment service repeats it up to 2 times with the same
  25| idempotency key. When Paylane PSP answers `authorized` instead of `challenge_required`, the
  26| payment skips steps 4 to 8 and continues at step 9.
  27| 
  28| #### 4.2.2 Table 4.3 — fields of `POST /payments`
  29| 
  30| | Field | Content |
  31| | :--- | :--- |
  32| | `order_id` | the order to pay |
  33| | `amount_minor` | the amount in minor currency units |
  34| | `currency` | the currency code |
  35| | `card_token` | the card, as a token from the payment form |
  36| | `billing_country` | the country of the billing address |
  37| | `device_fingerprint` | browser data for the risk check of the issuer |
  38| | `return_url` | the Checkout page address that the Issuer ACS returns to |
  39| | `idempotency_key` | one value for a request and all its repeats |
  40| | `customer_ip` | the IP address of the browser |
  41| 
  42| #### 4.2.3 Time limits
  43| 
  44| - The Payment service fails a payment that receives no webhook within 15 min.
  45| - Paylane PSP repeats an unanswered webhook every 5 min for up to 24 h.
  46| - The Orders API keeps the stock of an unpaid order reserved for 20 min.
=== END docs/specs/payments.md ===
